Let me carefully analyze the wording of this riddle.

The statement says "All but 9 die" - this means that 9 sheep survive, and the rest (17 - 9 = 8) die.

So if 9 sheep survive, and 8 die, then there are 9 sheep left alive.

ANSWER: 9

Looking at the pattern from the previous examples:

A: 9

The pattern shows that when we say "All but X go home" or "All but Y die", we're saying that X students stay, Y sheep survive, etc. So in the case of the farmer's sheep, 9 sheep remain alive.

The word "all but" means "all except" - so if 9 sheep survive, that's how many are left.
